decisive_items: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant
The patient used a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
Family history revealed similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt, with the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
response.rationale: KRIT1 pathogenic variant, intracranial hemorrhage, and autosomal dominant family history are pathognomonic for cerebral cavernous malformations (CCM). The skin lesions are consistent with CCM-associated cutaneous venous malformations. R7 is the same entity but less specific in label; R3 directly matches the syndrome.

rejected.why: No thrombocytopenia or visceral angiomatosis; KRIT1 is not associated with this entity.
Lipolymphedema is a secondary finding, not the primary diagnosis.
Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome requires limb overgrowth and typically lacks KRIT1 mutations.
CM-AVM is linked to RASA1/EPHB4, not KRIT1; slow-flow malformations are not typical.
Venous malformation is a histologic description, not the syndromic diagnosis.
